subject: series
synopsis: Annual issues for The Spectacular Spider-Man, featuring extended stories outside the regular run with guest stars, villains, and self-contained adventures for Marvel's most spectacular web-slinger.
author: Ralph Macchio, David Anthony Kraft

subject: series
synopsis: Michael Avon Oeming's dark superhero series about a vigilante group dealing with corrupt systems and personal demons.
author: Michael Avon Oeming

subject: series
synopsis: A man with nanite-enhanced blood and no memory of his true identity operates as a nearly indestructible killing machine; the series explored themes of identity and government exploitation and became one of Valiant's most enduring characters.
author: Duane Swierczynski

subject: series
synopsis: The graphic novel adaptation of the second A Song of Ice and Fire novel, following the War of the Five Kings across Westeros with multiple competing claimants to the throne.
author: Daniel Abraham

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Wagner's solo series. The original Claremont 4-issue mini is a charming swashbuckling adventure; the various ongoings are more variable.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Top Cow's 1996 The Darkness: mob hitman Jackie Estacado inherits a primordial demonic power on his 21st birthday; created by Garth Ennis, Marc Silvestri and David Wohl.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron and Russell Dauterman's 2014 Thor: a mysterious woman takes up Mjolnir after Odinson becomes unworthy, later revealed as Jane Foster.

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Latour's 2014 Wolverine and the X-Men: a powerless Logan headmasters the Jean Grey School while Quentin Quire faces a Phoenix-tinged future.
author: Jason Latour

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2007 12-issue revival of the Marvel Comics Presents anthology: serialized short features by rotating creators.

subject: series
synopsis: Melissa Flores' 2024 Boom! Studios relaunch of the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers comics.
author: Melissa Flores

subject: series
synopsis: Declan Shalvey's 2024 Mystique mini: Raven Darkholme on a covert mission after the fall of Krakoa.
author: Declan Shalvey

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's 1999 Angel ongoing tie-in to the TV series, opened by Christopher Golden.

subject: series
synopsis: Batman's annuals from 1961: reprint giants of 1950s stories, then new stories from the 1980s on.
author: Mike Baron, Robert Greenberger

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's 2012 X-Treme X-Men: an alternate Dazzler leads variant X-Men, including a younger Xavier, hunting evil Xaviers across realities.

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's 2012 Age of Apocalypse ongoing: the AoA reality's human resistance fights the Weapon X regime after Apocalypse's fall.

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Sheridan's 2023 limited series spotlighting Alan Scott, DC's original Green Lantern from the golden age, as he confronts a homophobic conspiracy tied to his history while explicitly honoring his identity as a gay man. A respectful and emotionally resonant treatment of one of DC's oldest heroes.
author: Tim Sheridan

subject: series
synopsis: Vertigo's 1994 mini-series spinning out of Swamp Thing, following a half-human creature born into the Un-Men. Dark body-horror with existential themes about belonging and monstrosity.
author: Dave Louapre

subject: series
synopsis: Kozue Amano's ARIA: apprentice gondolier Akari Mizunashi grows into her craft in Neo-Venezia on a terraformed Mars, a gentle healing slice-of-life.

subject: series
synopsis: The 2012 crossover event pitting the Avengers against the X-Men over the incoming Phoenix Force and Hope Summers, featuring the Phoenix Five gaining godlike power. Spectacular set pieces with an uneven narrative across five writers.
author: Jason Aaron, Brian Michael Bendis, Ed Brubaker, Jonathan Hickman, Matt Fraction

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King and David Marquez's 2022 heist series following Batman and Robin as they chase Catwoman and the Riddler across a compressed timeline involving a stolen artifact and Ra's al Ghul.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman and Tony Moore's anarchic debut sets a brawling, womanizing Pope against Hell's demons in a post-Rapture world, mixing irreverent blasphemy with genuine slapstick energy.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer and Riley Rossmo's Image series follows Fillmore Press — formerly the masked mass-murderer Madder Red — who, believing himself cured, offers to help police hunt a new killer. A tense psychological thriller about whether a monster can truly reform.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel limited series pairing Natasha Romanoff and Clint Barton on a shared espionage mission, leaning into the long friendship and professional respect between two of the Avengers' most grounded non-powered members.

subject: series
synopsis: Si Spencer's 2004 Vertigo series set in a parallel timeline where magic has sparked world war, following a grim version of Timothy Hunter navigating a magical apocalypse. An ambitious alternate-history expansion of the Books of Magic mythology that worked better as concept than execution.
author: Si Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: CrossGen's Celtic-warrior series by Chuck Dixon and Pablo Raimondi following Brath mac Gorm, a barbarian chieftain who leads his people against the Roman-equivalent Qesh Empire after receiving a sigil. A meat-and-potatoes historical fantasy entry in the CrossGen universe with solid art and straightforward adventure plotting.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2024 Conquest 2099 series set in the 2099 dystopian future timeline, following various heroes of that era in an expansion of the 2099 universe revival.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn and Juan Doe's series revealing that Noah's Ark had a dark counterpart carrying monsters and mythological creatures — a clever mythological horror premise.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Willingham's 2005 Infinite Crisis lead-in featuring the Spectre being manipulated into destroying magic, with the Shadowpact formed to oppose him. A solid if uncomplicated event tie-in.
author: Bill Willingham

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender and Wes Craig's series set at a secret school for the children of the world's most dangerous crime lords in 1980s San Francisco, following Marcus Lopez — a homeless teen recruited into the school — as he navigates brutal teen politics and assassination assignments.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Victor Gischler's comedic series assembling variants of Deadpool from across the multiverse — including Lady Deadpool, Headpool, Kidpool, and Dogpool — on a cosmic mission. Enjoyable but slight.
author: Victor Gischler

subject: series
synopsis: A Image/Skybound G.I. Joe villain-focused solo series exploring the arms dealer Destro's backstory and ambitions within the Skybound revival of the franchise.

subject: series
synopsis: Doctor Strange takes over Strange Tales' numbering (1968-1969): Roy Thomas and Gene Colan's moody, atmospheric run, cancelled at #183.

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' third year of their Tenth Doctor comics run, featuring the fan-favorite David Tennant incarnation in original adventures written for the comics medium. Part of the Lost Dimension crossover event and additional original stories showcasing the Tenth Doctor's emotional range and the charm that made him iconic.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Action Lab Entertainment's horror-comedy series following a vengeful doll-masked vigilante taking on crime and the supernatural with darkly humorous energy. A niche genre offering in the slasher-comedy tradition that developed a loyal following among fans of B-horror aesthetics.

subject: series
synopsis: David Greenberger and various artists' comics adaptation of interviews with elderly residents of a Boston nursing home — tender, funny, and profound oral history presented as vernacular comics.
author: David Greenberger

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel series presenting what is billed as a definitive chapter in Johnny Blaze's Ghost Rider saga — the Spirit of Vengeance at his most mythologically expansive.

subject: series
synopsis: Yu Aida's bittersweet action manga follows young girls turned into cyborg assassins for an Italian government agency, and the conflicted handlers who work with them. Praised for its melancholy exploration of the ethics of conditioning, childhood, and the cost of violence.
author: Yu Aida

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Ware's 2012 boxed graphic novel of fourteen booklets, broadsheets and pamphlets tracing the inhabitants of a Chicago brownstone, chiefly a lonely florist.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Agatha Harkness and her magical world in episodic adventures formatted for the Marvel Unlimited platform.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: W. Maxwell Prince and Martín Morazzo's anthology horror series with the Ice Cream Man as a malevolent narrator-of-vignettes. Each issue takes a different comics genre and horror of modern life and filters it through the Ice Cream Man's gleeful cruelty.
author: W. Maxwell Prince

subject: series
synopsis: Brandon Graham and Emma Rios' large-format comics anthology magazine featuring long-form serialized stories and single-issue experiments from a rotating cast of independent comics creators, dedicated to showcasing longer-format storytelling.
author: Brandon Graham, Emma Rios

subject: series
synopsis: Kelly Thompson and Sophie Campbell's 2015 IDW Jem and the Holograms: Jerrica Benton's band versus the Misfits, reimagined with warmth and style.

subject: series
synopsis: Tsutomu Nihei's (Blame!) hard sci-fi manga follows the last remnants of humanity aboard a massive seed ship battling alien creatures called Gauna. Notable for its uncompromising world-building, photorealistic mechanical design, and full-CG anime adaptation.
author: Tsutomu Nihei

subject: series
synopsis: Fuyumi Soryo's acclaimed shojo manga following Rei, a brooding motorcycle racer, and Kira, a shy artist, whose intensely passionate romance unfolds against trauma, violence, and psychological complexity rarely seen in the genre. Groundbreaking for shojo manga in its unflinching engagement with difficult themes and adult emotional realities.
author: Fuyumi Soryo

subject: series
synopsis: Created by Dean Motter, Mister X is the tormented architect of Radiant City, a psychetecture-designed metropolis that drives its inhabitants mad; a stylish, noir-influenced series with a distinctive retro-futurist visual aesthetic.
author: Dean Motter

subject: series
synopsis: Hideyuki Furuhashi and Betten Court's spinoff follows unlicensed vigilantes operating in the margins of the My Hero Academia world. Praised for its tighter pacing and more grounded character work compared to the main series.
author: Hideyuki Furuhashi

subject: series
synopsis: Part of Kazuo Koike and Goseki Kojima's Path of the Assassin series, following Hattori Hanzo's role as ninja bodyguard to the young Tokugawa Ieyasu as he maneuvers toward unifying Japan. Combines brutal action with political intrigue in the duo's signature gekiga style.
author: Kazuo Koike

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Michael Avon Oeming's third Powers arc follows Christian Walker as an agent for a federal bureau dedicated to superhuman crimes. Continues the series' blend of hard-boiled crime procedural and superhero deconstruction at Icon.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Yost's X-Men limited series follows Betsy Braddock investigating a Hand-connected mission that forces her to confront her own complex history of mind and body transformation. Focused character work with strong action sequences.
author: Chris Yost

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's Bronze Age anthology series featuring action-adventure stories drawn from the Marvel back catalogue, with a focus on characters like Moon Knight, Deathlok, and other darker Marvel protagonists.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Collected hardcover reprints of the classic Stan Lee and Jack Kirby war series featuring Nick Fury and the Howling Commandos during World War II. Essential for fans of Marvel's golden-age war comics.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Hiromu Arakawa's manga about a city kid who enrolls at an agricultural high school, discovering the hard realities of farming and animal husbandry. A gentle, deeply humane series from the creator of Fullmetal Alchemist, full of surprising emotional weight.
author: Arakawa Hiromu

subject: series
synopsis: Ron Marz and Ron Lim's nostalgic 2022 mini-series revisiting their classic early-1990s Silver Surfer run, pitting the Surfer and Thanos against a new cosmic threat. A warm reunion for the creative team that defined the cosmic Silver Surfer era.
author: Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV and Werther Dell'Edera's horror series: monster hunter Erica Slaughter arrives in Archer's Peak, where children are killed by creatures only they can see.
author: James Tynion IV, James Tynion

subject: series
synopsis: Tony Isabella's Bronze Age series featuring Daimon Hellstrom, son of Satan, as a reluctant supernatural hero, one of Marvel's attempts to capitalize on the horror boom of the early 1970s with occult superhero content.
author: Tony Isabella

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns's 1999 series introducing Courtney Whitmore as Star-Spangled Kid, fighting alongside her stepfather Pat Dugan in the STRIPE armor. A charming family superhero book and Johns's first major DC work.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: UDON Entertainment's continuation of their Street Fighter comics license, following the iconic fighting game characters across extended storylines. UDON's house art style and genuine affection for the games made their Street Fighter comics the best official treatment the franchise had received in print.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Peter B. Gillis's sci-fi series about humans who undergo a process granting superpowers to fight alien invaders — but the process kills them within a year. A dark, humanist war story that used its mortality premise for genuine emotional impact.
author: Peter B. Gillis

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1975-1977 series teaming Sub-Mariner and Doctor Doom as uneasy allies — two arrogant monarchs forced into partnership against greater threats. Peter Gillis and Tony Isabella explored the darkly comic tension between Marvel's most regal antagonists.
author: Tony Isabella

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2003 Thanos series: Jim Starlin's opening arc of the Mad Titan seeking redemption, then Keith Giffen's Samaritan arc leading into Annihilation.

subject: series
synopsis: A spin-off from Mike Allred's Madman universe featuring a team of atomic-powered heroes from Snap City in retro-cool superhero adventures full of pop art sensibility and Silver Age charm.
author: Mike Allred

subject: series
synopsis: Annual anthology of the year's finest comics work, guest-edited and drawn from across all genres and publishers — a reliable snapshot of the medium's diversity and ambition in 2016.

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Grant and Val Semeiks's 1990s ongoing for Etrigan the Demon, Jason Blood's rhyming hellspawn alter ego, featuring dark supernatural adventure and Grant's black humor.
author: Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV's 2021 DC series following Jim Gordon as he tracks the Joker across Europe on behalf of a mysterious employer, while the Joker himself plays cat-and-mouse across several parallel backup stories. A noir-inflected, psychologically probing take on Gotham's most iconic villain.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: The Baxter-format New Teen Titans (1984-1988): Wolfman and Pérez continue after the Judas Contract, then José Luis García-López and Eduardo Barreto.
author: Marv Wolfman, Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: A Spawn Universe team book featuring a group of supernatural heroes including characters from across the Spawn mythology banding together to protect Earth from demonic threats.

subject: series
synopsis: The Ben Grimm solo series from the mid-1980s follows the ever-lovin' blue-eyed Thing on adventures outside the Fantastic Four, including his stint as a professional wrestler. Later collected in omnibus format; captures Grimm's essential charm as Marvel's most lovable bruiser.
author: Mike Carlin

subject: series
synopsis: Library edition hardcover collecting the Dark Horse Witcher comics based on Andrzej Sapkowski's beloved fantasy series.

subject: series
synopsis: Sui Ishida's sequel follows amnesiac ghoul investigator Haise Sasaki whose buried past as Kaneki begins to resurface. A controversial continuation that divides fans while expanding the franchise's mythological scope.
author: Sui Ishida

subject: series
synopsis: Ahoy Comics' 2024 revival of Troma Entertainment's Toxic Avenger character, continuing the tradition of the radioactively mutated New Jersey hero fighting corruption and pollution with over-the-top grotesque violence and black humor. A respectful update of the cult property.
author: Matt Bors

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2012 True Blood ongoing tie-in to the HBO series, following Sookie Stackhouse and the vampires of Bon Temps.

subject: series
synopsis: Chuck Austen's Marvel MAX limited series recasting War Machine as a black-ops operative for hire in a harder-edged, more politically cynical take on James Rhodes. The MAX imprint's adult content allowances are used for grimmer military action.
author: Chuck Austen

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages anthology series retelling the origin stories of various X-Men characters and other Marvel heroes for younger readers, with simplified continuity and accessible art. A useful historical artifact but narratively thin.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's archival collected volumes of classic Warren Publishing Vampirella stories — the alien vampire from planet Drakulon in her original 1970s horror anthology format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A series of what-if scenarios spinning off from the Age of Ultron event, exploring alternate outcomes and butterfly-effect consequences of Wolverine's time-travel intervention.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Kiyohiko Azuma's universally beloved slice-of-life follows Yotsuba, an endlessly curious and energetic young girl, and her single father as she discovers ordinary wonders in her new neighborhood. Often cited as the most purely joyful manga ever made.
author: Kiyohiko Azuma

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's tie-in to the Avengers film. Accessible all-ages adventure deliberately aligned with the movie roster.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Rucka's 2014 series following the time-displaced teenage Scott Summers as he accompanies his father Corsair — a space pirate he never knew — through adventures across the cosmos, finally experiencing the childhood that was taken from him. A surprisingly warm father-son space adventure that gave the often-stoic Scott Summers rare room for joy and wonder.
author: Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: Chip Zdarsky's acclaimed Daredevil run in omnibus; modern noir-influenced narrative with exceptional character depth.
author: Chip Zdarsky

subject: series
synopsis: The 1976 series following Uncle Sam and a group of Quality Comics heroes—Human Bomb, Phantom Lady, Black Condor, the Ray, and Doll Man—fighting crime on Earth-X where the Nazis won WWII.
author: Bob Rozakis

subject: series
synopsis: Gilbert, Jaime and Mario Hernandez's original 1982-1996 Love and Rockets: Jaime's Locas and Gilbert's Palomar, the landmark of alternative comics.
author: Gilbert Hernandez, Mario Hernandez

subject: series
synopsis: Sean McKeever's underseen limited series follows Juston Seyfert, a teenage boy who repairs a damaged Sentinel robot and forms an unlikely bond with it — a surprisingly tender character study of identity and trust wrapped in superhero action.
author: Sean McKeever

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Valentino's Image title about an HIV-positive anti-hero. Noble intentions hampered by the era's excess — the social messaging lands harder than the storytelling.
author: Jim Valentino

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's 2014 solo series restoring Ororo Munroe to her African roots and wanderer identity, exploring her relationship with the people she protects and questioning her place between the X-Men and the wider world.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and Darick Robertson's cyberpunk political satire following gonzo journalist Spider Jerusalem as he wages war on a corrupt future America. Visionary, furious, and prescient.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Alex Raymond's elegantly drawn newspaper detective strip about Rip Kirby, a pipe-smoking former OSS agent turned private investigator. Raymond's sophisticated linework set a visual standard for the adventure strip; after his death in 1956, John Prentice continued the strip with comparable craft until 1999.
author: Alex Raymond

subject: series
synopsis: Aleš Kot and Michael Walsh's 2014 Secret Avengers: Maria Hill's S.H.I.E.L.D. black-ops team with Coulson, Hawkeye and Black Widow in an absurdist spy comedy.

subject: series
synopsis: Amanda Conner and Jimmy Palmiotti's 2013 Harley Quinn: Harley moves to Coney Island, runs a boarding house of misfits and finds her antihero voice in a slapstick run.

subject: series
synopsis: Doug Moench and Bill Sienkiewicz's 1980 Moon Knight: Marc Spector juggles identities as mercenary, millionaire and cabbie while Sienkiewicz's art turns revolutionary.

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder and Jim Cheung's 2018 Justice League: the League against Lex Luthor's Legion of Doom and Perpetua, then Venditti and Williamson.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2004 Spider-Man Unlimited anthology of short Spider-Man stories by rotating creators.

subject: series
synopsis: The Authority volume 2 (2003-2004): Robbie Morrison and Dwayne Turner's post-Millar run, as the team grapples with the world they reshaped.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Cornell and Alan Davis's 2013 Wolverine: a Logan without his healing factor faces a body-hopping killer.

subject: series
synopsis: Eagle Comics' 1983 US reprints of 2000 AD's Judge Dredd, coloured and reformatted: Wagner and Grant's Mega-City One stories for American readers.

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Orlando's 2024 Annihilation 2099 mini-series in Marvel's 2099 future.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David and David Lopez's 2003 Fallen Angel: Lee, a mysterious avenging woman, operates in the corrupt city of Bete Noire; later continued at IDW.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's New Avengers, here the 2006-2007 stretch (#16-30) through Civil War's fallout.

subject: series
synopsis: Takahiro and Tetsuya Tashiro's dark fantasy: country boy Tatsumi joins Night Raid, an assassin squad killing the Empire's corrupt elite.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's golden-age Flash anthology originally published 1941–1947, collecting prose and comics stories of Jay Garrick the Flash. A historically significant title as one of DC's first character-dedicated anthology magazines, later revived for special issues. Important for golden-age Flash fans and comics historians.
author: Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: Infinity Comics vertical-scroll adaptation of Dan Slott and Olivier Coipel's 2014 Spider-Verse arc from The Amazing Spider-Man #9-15.

subject: series
synopsis: James Kochalka's daily diary comic strip — running from 1998 to 2012 — documenting his everyday life with his family in Burlington, Vermont, through tiny four-panel strips. A foundational work of autobiographical webcomics and one of the most sustained daily-comic projects in the medium.
author: James Kochalka

subject: series
synopsis: Osamu Tezuka-inspired manga prequel exploring the origin of Astro Boy's world — Tetsuro Kasahara and Masami Yuuki's prequel to Tetsuwan Atom (Astro Boy).
author: Masami Yuuki

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Clevinger and Scott Wegener's joyful action-adventure follows Atomic Robo, an atomic-powered robot created by Nikola Tesla in 1923, fighting through adventures spanning the entire 20th and 21st centuries.
author: Brian Clevinger

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns, Jeff Katz and Dan Jurgens' 2007 Booster Gold: secretly guarding the timeline with Rip Hunter while the world thinks him a fame-hungry joke.

subject: series
synopsis: John Layman and Rob Guillory's comedic crime series following Tony Chu, an FDA agent who is cibopath — he gets psychic impressions from anything he eats. In a world where alcohol is legal but chicken is Prohibition-banned, Tony investigates food crimes for a secret government agency.
author: John Layman

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's 2016 Dark Horse Conan the Slayer: the Cimmerian among Kozaki raiders, then an adaptation of Howard's The Devil in Iron.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Ted Naifeh's gothic fantasy series about a surly girl who moves to a creepy old house and discovers her uncle is a warlock, mixing fairy-tale darkness with suburban alienation.
author: Ted Naifeh

subject: series
synopsis: A 2023-2024 Daredevil story arc following Matt Murdock with a new suit and renewed mission, exploring the intersection of Daredevil's vigilante code and the increasingly brutal world around him.

subject: series
synopsis: Victor Gischler's deliberately irreverent Deadpool series featuring 'Head-Pool,' a zombie version of the Merc with a Mouth, in a horror-parody adventure that leaned into Deadpool's fourth-wall-breaking humor and gleeful grotesquery.
author: Victor Gischler

subject: series
synopsis: Ryoko Kui's fantasy manga about an adventuring party that survives a dungeon by cooking and eating the monsters they encounter. Combines meticulous culinary worldbuilding with genuine character depth and thoughtful exploration of ecological interdependence.
author: Ryoko Kui

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' Eleventh Doctor series concludes with the Lost Dimension crossover event, bringing Matt Smith's beloved portrayal to a fitting comics end. Strong production values, original companion characters, and tonal fidelity to the Moffat era distinguish these Titan titles as genuine companion pieces to the TV series.
author: Si Spurrier

subject: series
synopsis: The closing arc of Titan's Twelfth Doctor comics captures Peter Capaldi's steely, philosophical Doctor in a send-off incorporating the multi-Doctor Lost Dimension event. Reliable licensed work with a genuine understanding of Capaldi's characterization and the darker, more introspective tone of his era.
author: Richard Dinnick

subject: series
synopsis: Spider-Verse event exploring the society of spider-powered individuals.

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's conclusion to the Krakoa era, depicting the fall of the mutant nation-state and Orchis's offensive against mutantkind, bookending the Hickman-initiated era with significant status quo changes.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2011 post-Fear Itself limited series by Matt Fraction, Christos Gage, and Cullen Bunn following the war over the fear hammers that were scattered across Earth during the event, with Valkyrie racing against Sinister Twelve agents to collect them. A solid Fear Itself epilogue.
author: Matt Fraction, Christos Gage, Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's series reviving the Valkyrior concept through Valkyrie and Misty Knight assembling an all-female team, mixing Norse mythology with superhero action and feminist themes though cut short after 12 issues.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Comics adaptation of Frank Frazetta's iconic Death Dealer painting — the mysterious, skull-helmed horseman whose image has defined dark fantasy art for decades. Multiple publishers have taken runs at the property; Opus Comics' 2022 version sought to finally do justice to the painting's raw power in long-form storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Devil's Due/Image's early-2000s G.I. Joe reboot stripped away the codenames and colorful costumes in favor of a contemporary special forces aesthetic, reimagining Cobra as a credible 21st-century terrorist network. Realistic in tone but lacking the original's personality.
author: John Ney Rieber

subject: series
synopsis: Tsujitomo's (art) and Masaya Tsunamoto's (story) manga about Tatsumi Take, an unconventional soccer coach who returns to rebuild the struggling East Tokyo United club. A sophisticated sports manga focused as much on team management, tactics, and psychology as on match action — one of the most realistic and thoughtful soccer manga.
author: Tsujitomo, Masaya Tsunamoto

subject: series
synopsis: Sun Takeda's dark action-mystery follows a high school boy who can transform into a monster suit and the girl who wears him, hunting alien coins with increasingly disturbing revelations. Notorious for extreme violence and boundary-pushing content.
author: Sun Takeda

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' anthology reprint series collecting Golden Age superhero material from the public domain, preserving early American superhero comics featuring characters like Phantom Lady, the Black Terror, and Captain Courageous. An invaluable archival project for Golden Age collectors and comics historians.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dave Gibbons' 2005 limited series relaunching the Green Lantern Corps with Guy Gardner and Kyle Rayner rebuilding the intergalactic peacekeeping force following Green Lantern Rebirth. A solid corporate superhero series elevated by Gibbons' craft and the appealing dynamic between the two very different Lanterns.
author: Dave Gibbons

subject: series
synopsis: A collected edition of Hexed, the supernatural adventure following Luci Jennifer Inacio Das Neves, a thief who steals magical artifacts.
author: Michael Alan Nelson

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's digital-first Injustice prequel set during WWII, following the Justice Society of America's original heroes at the dawn of the superhero age. Expands the Injustice universe's history while delivering the same sharp character work as Taylor's main series.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: Daruma Matagi's dark psychological thriller follows Kasane, a disfigured daughter of a legendary beauty actress, who discovers a lipstick that lets her swap faces with others, using it to pursue her mother's theatrical legacy. A compelling meditation on beauty, identity, and the price of borrowed talent.
author: Daruma Matagi

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen and J.M. DeMatteis's 2013 ongoing comedic series starring Larfleeze, the singular member of the Orange Lantern Corps and embodiment of avarice in DC's emotional spectrum. The creative team leaned fully into the absurdist possibilities of a Scrooge-like alien driven entirely by want, making it one of DC's more unexpected character vehicles.
author: Keith Giffen, J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages retelling of Iron Man adventures for younger readers, presenting Tony Stark's exploits in self-contained stories appropriate for children. Part of the Marvel Adventures imprint that reimagined Marvel heroes for an all-ages audience.

subject: series
synopsis: A collectible figurine magazine series featuring Marvel characters as chess pieces, with each issue providing a figure and background information about the character — a part-work publication rather than a traditional comic.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages adaptation of the Avengers Assemble animated series, presenting kid-friendly Avengers adventures in digest format. Part of Marvel's broad all-ages line of animated tie-in comics targeting younger readers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages companion to the Avengers Assemble animated series second season, adapting or complementing stories from the show for young readers who want comics alongside the cartoon.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire's 2024 Boom! series: a small-town tarot reader returns home to care for her ailing mother and finds her own psychic gift is real.

subject: series
synopsis: ONE's webcomic about a powerful middle-school psychic who wants nothing more than to live an ordinary life. Deceptively simple art concealing sophisticated character work and genuine emotional sincerity beneath absurdist comedy.
author: ONE

subject: series
synopsis: A DC Comics crossover event series tied to the MultiVersus video game, featuring Warner Bros. characters from across properties including DC heroes, Looney Tunes, and other WB franchises in a multiverse-spanning conflict.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1967 humor anthology parodying superhero comics, featuring parodies of its own characters (Forbush Man, Spidey-Man) by creators including Stan Lee, Roy Thomas, and Marie Severin. A fascinating artifact of Marvel's self-awareness at its Silver Age peak.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: A Marvel reference publication indexing the publisher's comics by character — tracking first appearances, major story arcs, and key issues in systematic detail. An invaluable resource for continuity research rather than an entertainment comic.

subject: series
synopsis: Adrian Tomine's long-running anthology series collecting his meticulously observed slice-of-life short stories and novellas about modern loneliness, identity, and interpersonal miscommunication.
author: Adrian Tomine

subject: series
